aiOverview.content: As of April 2, 2026, President Trump has fired Pam Bondi as Attorney General, appointing Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche as the acting Attorney General. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Administrator Lee Zeldin is considered the frontrunner to replace her permanently, though others are also under consideration. Key details regarding the transition: Interim Successor: Todd Blanche, who served as Trump's defense attorney in several criminal cases, will take over leadership of the Department of Justice (DOJ) immediately as acting attorney general. Permanent Replacement Candidates: Lee Zeldin is considered the top choice and has reportedly been in discussions with Trump, though other names, including Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton and Sen. Mike Lee (R-Utah), have been mentioned. Reason for Firing: Trump was reportedly dissatisfied with Bondi's handling of DOJ files related to Jeffrey Epstein and her perceived lack of prosecution of his political opponents. Bondi’s Next Move: Trump announced that Bondi will be transitioning to a position in the private sector. Bondi's departure follows a tumultuous tenure and increased pressure from Congress regarding her management of the DOJ.
